content:
A new open-source tool has recently sparked heated discussion, claiming to allow users who are not interested in Apple Intelligence to reclaim 12GB or more of storage space on their Mac. Details are as follows.

"Disable Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove downloaded models"

Like many companies that have added various AI tools and models to their platforms, Apple has faced criticism for features that some users consider superfluous and that take up storage space.

Apple Intelligence originally required up to 7GB of storage on macOS 26, but with macOS 27 this figure has increased significantly, with Apple now saying its latest models may require up to 14GB of space on newer Macs.

In response, independent developer Om Lahore published a project called RemoveMacAI on GitHub late last week, claiming it can "disable Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove downloaded models".

Lahore explains that his tool can enable a configuration profile that applies Apple's own restriction keys to turn off Apple Intelligence features, while using the company's asset services to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.

He also details in detail what the tool will remove, which features will be disabled, and what users can expect after running it:

Disabled features: Siri (including "Hey Siri" and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, ChatGPT extensions, summaries for Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes and Notifications, Mail smart replies, inline text prediction, Spatial Photos, the Photos Clean Up tool, and Xcode predictive code completion. Removed models: Apple Intelligence foundation models, as well as models for image generation and Genmoji, Spatial Photos, the Photos Clean Up tool, and Xcode code completion.

and

Lahore notes that Dictation will still work after running RemoveMacAI, because "Dictation is a separate setting, and its language model is not removed".

Finally, he adds that the entire process is reversible, with full details and instructions available here.

9to5Mac's take

Although some of the strong backlash against Apple Intelligence taking up storage space on Mac seems little different from an instinctive aversion to anything AI-related, for users with limited internal storage—especially those with a 256GB Mac—reclaiming 12GB or more is a legitimate concern.

There is also a more fundamental issue of basic control over one's own operating system: users who are not interested in Apple Intelligence should be able to easily turn it off completely and reclaim the storage space used by its models, just as they can manage other apps or optional components within the system.

That said, it remains to be seen whether Apple will try to take the project down from GitHub, or change the underlying mechanisms of macOS to make Apple Intelligence models more difficult to remove.

Similarly, it is also impossible to know what impact disabling or removing these components will have on macOS itself—or even on third-party apps that increasingly rely on Apple models to provide basic functionality.

Although RemoveMacAI is open source and does not require disabling System Integrity Protection (SIP), it still relies on configuration profiles, restriction keys, and system services that Apple can change at any time.

In other words, future macOS updates may cause some of the tool's features to stop working, and may even cause users to experience unexpected behaviour until the project is updated.

For now, anyone considering using RemoveMacAI should understand that this is an unofficial third-party tool that makes system-level changes, and should be comfortable with how it works.

To be clear, RemoveMacAI appears to be a well-intentioned open-source project aimed at giving Mac users more autonomy and control over what runs on their computers and how their storage is used. It is just impossible to know whether Apple will view it the same way.
